target_customer: Plaintiff law firms running class action and mass tort cases
problem: Qualifying thousands of claimants means reading thousands of pages of medical, financial and employment records; Kalinda extracts and aggregates that data with AI.
business_model: B2B software subscriptions or per case fees to law firms (pricing not stated)
product_category: Legal AI for mass tort record review

founders.name: Sayan Bhatia
previous_startups: Co-founded a STEM nonprofit reaching 7,000 students
founders.background_notes: YC launch post says the lab is at UC Davis. Brother of the CTO.

founders.name: Sohil Bhatia
founders.background_notes: Brother of the CEO per the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Extracting structured facts from long, messy medical and employment records with high accuracy is demanding, but it builds on LLM document tools; the founders are AI researchers from academic and national lab settings per the YC page.

defensibility.rationale: Several legal AI vendors already served plaintiff firms; integration into large litigation workflows and accuracy track record would be the moat.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: A search found other mass tort record review tools (Supio and Angeion's EvidenceEngine among them) but undated, so no dated competitor list is recorded. No acquisition of Kalinda found.

market_need_then: Mass tort firms process thousands of claimants per case. The founders reported 600k pages processed and an interview in September 2025 reported about $60K revenue in four months from three large plaintiff firms (company reported).

branding.domain_note: Uses kalinda.ai; no purchase story found.

identity.logo: Not described by any source found
identity.visual_style: Minimal landing page with only a title and tagline when fetched
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct sales tagline signs your next case

branding.community_and_virality: A podcast episode (Law, AI and Money) featured the founders; no merch or fan activity found.

brand_strength.rationale: A distinctive short name but no source shows brand awareness; the name is also a common given name, which a baby name site says derives from Sanskrit, but nothing connects that to the company.

outcome_analysis: Kalinda is active and early, a two founder team that reports live deployments at large plaintiff firms and early revenue. No acquisition, shutdown or layoffs were found. Funding is thinly documented, and competition from other legal AI vendors is the main risk, so the story is too early to read.
notes: Unverified funding: Caplight lists a seed dated 2026-04-09 with S28 Capital and Y Combinator as investors and total $500K, later $692K; no company confirmation. No round recorded. Customer count differs between the YC launch (2 firms) and the September 2025 interview (3 firms). Competitor list empty because found sources were undated. Education not found. Completeness pass: the seed rests on a single database (Caplight); totals of 500K, 692K and 1.2M conflict across aggregators, so no amount is recorded.
